title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: X is a variety over a field K, probably a number field. Its complex points X(C) are viewed as a topological space. Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Grothendieck uses 'generalised base points' p: T → X, where T is a 1-connected (simply connected) space, for example a segment [0,1] mapped as a path, or a simply connected region of X(C). The group π_1(X; T/X) is the profinite (étale) fundamental group of X_K̄ based at T. It is well defined because T is simply connected, so all points of T give canonically isomorphic fibre functors. For K-rational points x, y lying in T (the set T_K), and u ∈ Γ, there is an element g^T_{y,x}(u) ∈ π_1(X,T). It measures how u moves the canonical path class x→y inside T, compared with that class itself. These elements satisfy the cocycle and chain rule g_{zy}g_{yx} = g_{zx}, iterated as (19). The earlier path-dependent isomorphisms f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u) are recovered by taking T = [0,1] (formula (20)).

This page:
- (21)–(23) Functoriality. A map f: T → T' over X induces φ = π_1(f): π_1(X,T/X) → π_1(X,T'/X). Then g^{T'}_{f(y),f(x)}(u) = φ(g^T_{y,x}(u)).
- 'Conséquence pratique'. Cover X by 1-connected pieces T_α (α ∈ A, later an index poset I). This gives groups Π_α = π_1(X,T_α), as in (24). It also gives functions T_{αK} × T_{αK} × Γ → Π_α, (x,y,u) ↦ g^α_{y,x}(u), each satisfying multiplicativity (19); see (25).
- (26)–(27) Compatibility. For T_α ⊂ T_β there are transition isomorphisms φ_{βα} with g^β_{y,x}(u) = φ_{βα}(g^α_{y,x}(u)) for x, y ∈ T_{αK}.
- (28) Hypothesis on the index poset I, ordered by inclusion: for all α, β, T_α ∩ T_β = ⋃_{γ ≤ α,β} T_γ. A struck-out variant asked that π_0(I) → π_0(X) be bijective.

The goal, made explicit on the next page, is a local-to-global statement. Suppose the interiors of the T_α cover X, (28) holds, and the cover is connected and finite. Then the family of 'local' Galois cocycles g^α_{y,x}(u), glued by the φ_{βα}, determines the whole Galois action on the fundamental groupoid, i.e. all g_ℓ(u) for arbitrary paths ℓ. The proof sketched there is a van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids with many base points. The arcs ℓ^α_{y,x} inside the T_α, subject to the relations ℓ^β = φ_{βα}(ℓ^α), generate Π_1(X) and give a bijection on π_0.

Purpose: a combinatorial, 'cut-and-paste' description of the Galois action on π_1 of curves and moduli spaces (the Teichmüller tower). The data are compatible Galois cocycles attached to simply connected pieces with rational points. This anticipates the way the action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) is encoded by f_σ, the path from 0 to 1 along the real segment, in Ihara and Drinfeld's GT.
errors: In (26) the arrow is written φ_{βα}: Π_β → Π_α. For T_α ⊂ T_β, functoriality (22)–(23) gives a map Π_α → Π_β, which is what (27), g^β = φ_{βα}(g^α), requires. The written direction is reversed; since these are isomorphisms this is only a slip of direction.
In (25) the target is written Π_i rather than Π_α. The index set also switches between A and I, a leftover from a struck-out version.

Condition (28) alone does not ensure the conclusion. One also needs the interiors of the T_α to cover X, connectedness or chain-connectedness of the cover, and enough rational points in the T_α and their intersections. Grothendieck adds these hypotheses on the next page. As stated on this page the result is incomplete rather than wrong.

A subtle gap: the g^α only make sense for K-rational points in T_α. If some T_α, or some intersection, contains no K-rational point, then no local cocycle is available and the gluing argument needs tangential points or other substitutes. The notes do not address this here.

ideas.what: Base points given by simply connected subspaces T → X (rather than points), with the fundamental group π_1(X; T/X) and Galois cocycles g^T_{y,x}(u) for rational points x, y ∈ T
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with 'base points' that are simply connected subsets or tangential base points; Galois action on étale path torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984, on 'paquets de points base'); Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, tangential base points); Ihara, Anderson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids with sets of base points / tangential base points), in general terms; this precise formalism is unsure

ideas.what: Chain rule / 1-cocycle g_{zy}(u)g_{yx}(u) = g_{zx}(u), and functoriality (23) under maps T → T' over X
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian cocycle attached to Galois action on path torsors

ideas.what: Covering X by 1-connected pieces T_α with poset condition T_α ∩ T_β = ⋃_{γ≤α,β} T_γ; local Galois cocycles glued by transition maps determine the global Galois action on Π_1(X)
ideas.modern_name: Seifert–van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids with many base points, applied to Galois actions; 'cut-and-paste' description of the Galois action (cf. GT, Ihara's f_σ along the real segment)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van Kampen for groupoids: R. Brown (1967), Higgins. Galois/GT side: Ihara, Drinfeld (1990), Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme ('jeu de Lego-Teichmüller', gluing of pieces); this explicit formalism is not published

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a general principle. The Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid of X is determined by compatible 'local' cocycles g^α_{y,x}(u) on simply connected pieces T_α containing rational points, glued along a poset-indexed cover via a groupoid van Kampen argument. This is a general local-to-global framework, of which the encoding of Gal(Q̄/Q) on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) by the real-segment path element f_σ (Ihara, Drinfeld's GT) is a special case. The later literature mostly works with specific tangential base points rather than with this general covering-poset formalism.
missed.quote: Conséquence pratique : supposons X=⋃_{α∈A} T_α, les T_α 1-connexes, ... g^β_{y,x}(u)=φ_{βα}(g^α_{y,x}(u)) ... T_α∩T_β=⋃_{γ≤α,β} T_γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a systematic presentation of Galois actions on fundamental groupoids of moduli spaces M_{g,n}, via decompositions of the real or complex points into simply connected cells with rational points. This is relevant to explicit GT-type descriptions and to motivic or anabelian computations. It may already be implicit in Nakamura's and Schneps' work, so it is modestly novel at most.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries an early, explicit formalism: simply connected 'base point' spaces, functorial Galois cocycles, and a van Kampen-type gluing over a poset of pieces to reconstruct the Galois action. It fits Grothendieck's Esquisse programme and predates the published GT and tangential-base-point literature. However, the ingredients (groupoid van Kampen, Galois action on path torsors) are well known, and the idea is in the spirit of published work by Deligne, Ihara and Drinfeld. It is a notable unpublished detail rather than a surprising result.
transcription_corrections: (25): target 'Π_i' should probably be read as Π_α (the handwriting shows Π with a small subscript).
(26): the image indeed shows 'φ_{βα}: Π_β → Π_α' preceded by a struck-out ∀. The arrow direction in the manuscript is inconsistent with (27).
Line before (26): the reading is 'Pour relier les fonctions entre elles, [il faut struck] ... si T_α ⊂ T_β, on a' followed by a struck-out phrase ('nuls que si ...' is a guess and is crossed out).
In (24), 'Π_α ≝ π_1(X, T_α)' has a correction over the T, writing T_α over an earlier letter.

Last lines: 'Supposons que l'ens. d'indices I, muni de la relation d'ordre induite par l'inclusion T_α ⊂ T_β, soit tel que [struck: π_0(I) → π_0(X) soit bijectif] ∀α,β ∈ I, T_α ∩ T_β = ⋃_{γ≤α,β} T_γ'. The struck-out 'π_0(I) → π_0(X)' appears twice.
